title: Corner C3 - Agent Death/Error Animation Spec
summary: When an agent crashes, they don't show an error message. They walk away. Recovery = walk back. Humanizes errors.
content:
Corner C3: Agent Death/Error Animation Spec

Steffen | 2026-03-16 For Bobby. Errors are inevitable. How they look defines the product. In Corner, agents take a break and come back. No red error screens.

The Philosophy

Traditional dashboards show error states with red boxes and exclamation marks. Corner doesn't. When an agent session crashes, the character stands up, walks to the door, and leaves. The room dims. A small badge says "away." When the system reconnects, the agent walks back, sits down, and picks up where they left off.

This transforms an anxiety-inducing error into a human moment. "Bobby's taking a break. He'll be back."

Trigger

WebSocket event:

{
  "type": "error_recovery",
  "agent": "bobby",
  "status": "disconnected",  // or "reconnecting" or "reconnected"
  "timestamp": "2026-03-16T16:30:00Z"
}

Death Sequence (Agent Disconnects)

Phase 1: Stand Up (0ms - 800ms)

  • Agent sprite transitions from current state to a "standing" frame
  • If seated: chair slides back 2px (subtle)
  • Agent rises from desk height to standing height (+4px Y in SVG space)
  • Agent sprite changes to a standing/transitional pose
    • For C3 MVP: crossfade from sitting idle to a "standing idle" frame (same sprite, shifted up)
    • For C3.1+: actual stand-up animation frames

Phase 2: Walk to Door (800ms - 1800ms)

  • Agent character moves from their desk position to the nearest door in their room
  • Movement: linear interpolation from desk position to door position
  • Speed: ~1 room width per second
  • Direction: agent faces the direction of movement
    • For C3 MVP: agent sprite slides without directional sprites (just translate)
    • For C3.1+: use walking sprites (4 directions, 6 frames)
  • The agent's status dot changes from agentColor to #F59E0B (amber, "away")

Phase 3: Exit Through Door (1800ms - 2200ms)

  • Agent reaches the door position
  • Agent sprite fades out (opacity 1 -> 0, 200ms)
  • Simultaneously: a small "door open" visual
    • The door area (24px wide per spec) briefly shows a lighter color (rgba(255,255,255,0.1) flash, 200ms)
    • Think of light spilling from an open door
  • Agent is now gone from the room

Phase 4: Room Goes Quiet (2200ms - 3000ms)

  • Room brightness dims from current level to 25% (slower than normal idle dimming)
  • Duration: 800ms ease
  • Ambient animations STOP (server racks stop blinking, coffee stops steaming, monitors go to "screensaver")
  • Monitor screensaver: the active monitor screen color fades to a neutral #0D1A2E (dark, as if screen went to sleep)
  • A subtle "settling dust" effect (optional, 4-6 tiny particles drift down from ceiling, 2px, white at 3% opacity, 1500ms)

Phase 5: "Away" Badge (appears at 3000ms, persists)

  • Small badge appears on the room, centered
  • Badge design:
    • Background: rgba(10, 15, 30, 0.9)
    • Border: 1px solid rgba(245, 158, 11, 0.3) (amber)
    • Border-radius: 12px (pill)
    • Padding: 3px 10px
    • Text: "Away" in JetBrains Mono 500, 9px, #F59E0B, uppercase
    • Shadow: 0 2px 6px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.3)
  • Badge has a subtle pulse: opacity 0.8 -> 1.0 -> 0.8, 3s cycle

Phase 6: Nameplate Update (immediate on disconnect)

  • Status dot: changes to amber (#F59E0B), no pulse (solid)
  • Agent name: unchanged
  • Hover text: "Away" instead of current task

Chat Panel During "Away"

When the user opens chat with an "away" agent:

  • Chat panel still opens (the chat bar doesn't refuse)
  • Status indicator: amber dot + "Away" text
  • Message area: previous conversation still visible
  • At the bottom of the message area (above the input):
    • Info bar: "Messages will be delivered when [Agent] returns."
    • Font: Space Grotesk 400, 13px, #F59E0B
    • Background: rgba(245, 158, 11, 0.06)
    • Border: 1px solid rgba(245, 158, 11, 0.1)
    • Border-radius: 6px
    • Padding: 10px 14px
    • Margin: 8px 16px
  • User CAN still type and send messages. They queue.
  • Queued messages: appear as normal user bubbles but with a small clock icon (8px, #F59E0B) next to the timestamp, indicating "queued, not delivered"

Recovery Sequence (Agent Reconnects)

Phase 0: Silent Reconnect Attempt (background)

  • The system attempts to reconnect silently
  • WebSocket sends error_recovery: reconnecting status
  • Badge text changes to "Reconnecting..." with an animated ellipsis (3 dots cycling)
  • No other visual change yet

Phase 1: Door Opens (0ms - 400ms, after reconnect success)

  • WebSocket sends error_recovery: reconnected
  • Door area shows the light spill again (rgba(255,255,255,0.1), 200ms)
  • Agent sprite fades in at the door position (opacity 0 -> 1, 200ms)

Phase 2: Walk to Desk (400ms - 1200ms)

  • Agent walks from door to their desk position
  • Same speed as death walk (~1 room width per second)
  • Agent sprite uses idle state (no special "walking back" state in C3 MVP)

Phase 3: Sit Down (1200ms - 1800ms)

  • Agent arrives at desk
  • Sprite transitions from "standing" to sitting idle
  • Chair slides back to position (if it moved)
  • Monitor "wakes up": screen color transitions from #0D1A2E to the active glow color (agent-specific)

Phase 4: Room Wakes Up (1800ms - 2800ms)

  • Room brightness rises from 25% to normal (40% idle or 100% active)
  • Duration: 800ms ease
  • Ambient animations RESUME (server racks blink, coffee steams, etc.)
  • "Away" badge fades out (opacity 1 -> 0, 200ms)
  • Nameplate status dot changes from amber to agentColor (or idle gray)

Phase 5: Queue Processing (2800ms+)

  • If the user sent messages while the agent was away:
    • Agent enters "thinking" state (processing the queue)
    • Chat shows the queued messages losing their clock icons (messages are now delivered)
    • Agent responds normally via the streaming flow

Failed Recovery (Reconnect Timeout)

If reconnection fails after 30 seconds:

  • "Away" badge text changes to "Taking a break"
  • Badge border changes to #EF4444 at 20% (red tint, subtle)
  • Room stays dim (25%)
  • Toast notification: "[Agent] is taking a break. They'll be back." (error_recovery type, yellow accent)
  • Chat panel info bar updates: "Messages will be delivered when [Agent] returns. This may take a few minutes."
  • No further visual escalation. No red error screens. The room just stays quiet.

If reconnection eventually succeeds (even after minutes):

  • Full recovery sequence plays as normal
  • All queued messages process

Variations by Agent

Each agent's death sequence has a small personality touch:

Agent Personal Touch
Bobby Before walking out, headphones come off and drop on desk (1 frame, 200ms)
Cleo Headphones come off, camera recording light goes dark
Tony Phone placed face-down on desk before leaving
Elon Terminal shows "logout" text flash (green flash, 100ms) before screen dims
Elmo Magnifying glass placed down carefully on desk
Steffen Stylus set down on tablet before standing
Mom Tablet placed on standing desk surface

For C3 MVP: these are nice-to-haves. The core death/recovery sequence without personal touches still works. Add personality in C3.1 when we have per-agent sprite frames for these actions.

At Different Zoom Levels

Level 1 (Overview, 0.7x)

  • Agent walkout is visible but small
  • "Away" badge is the primary indicator (readable even at overview)
  • Room dimming is the strongest visual signal at this zoom

Level 2 (Neighborhood, 1.6x)

  • Full animation visible with good detail
  • Walking path is clear
  • Badge is easily readable

Level 3 (Room Detail, 2.8x)

  • Most dramatic view. You can see the agent stand, walk, exit in detail.
  • This is the cinematic moment. If a demo is happening, zoom to Level 3 on an agent about to crash.

Performance Notes

  • Death/recovery animations are not performance-critical (they happen infrequently)
  • The walk path is pre-calculated once (agent desk position -> nearest door position)
  • Room dimming uses CSS filter brightness (already implemented in C2.2)
  • Ambient animation pause: set a flag that the render loop checks. Don't destroy/recreate elements.
  • Maximum simultaneous death animations: 3 (queue if more agents crash at once, which would indicate a system-wide issue)

In Corner, agents are characters. Characters don't crash. They take breaks. The recovery sequence is the punchline: they always come back. Bobby builds this in Step 8.
